title: IELTS Academic 20 - Listening Test 3 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

16:09ANNOUNCER: Part 3. You will hear two theatre studies students, Maya and Finn, discussing their project on theatre programmes.
16:20ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 26.
17:10ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26.
17:18MAYA: So Finn, I've done as much as I can for our project on theatre programs. How's your research coming along?
17:26FINN: Okay, Maya. I didn't know theatre programs are called playbills in the USA till I started looking into the topic. Even though I struggled to find many useful websites, I'm glad we picked this subject. No one else on the course is doing the same as us, although it is one of the research areas of the module convener. That might actually put some people off.
17:50MAYA: I suppose so. Anyway, I hadn't realised there are actually companies specialising in creating theatre programmes.
17:57FINN: Yes, they're quite common nowadays.
18:00MAYA: Contrary to what many people think, theatres don't hire people to do the programmes. In fact, companies buy the rights to publish programmes on the theatre's behalf, and then make their money selling advertising space within the programme booklet.
18:15FINN: It must be easier for theatres to do it that way. Yes. I remember reading something about programmes in early British theatre. It said that the cast was always very important.
18:26MAYA: Yeah. Audiences were very familiar with leading actors and big names would draw huge crowds.
18:33FINN: But I hadn't realised that if the programme named a famous actor, that's who the public expected to perform. And if that didn't happen, people accused the theatre of breaking their agreement with the audience. They would demand refunds, and if they didn't get them, there were riots.
18:51MAYA: Outrageous! That had never happened now. People are too polite. Even when they're disappointed if the star of the show misses a performance. We should definitely include that information about early audiences in our project. I also think it's important to mention that lots of ordinary people at that time were illiterate, so theatre programmes were of limited value in advertising plays. When a company of actors arrived in a town, they'd parade around the streets in their costumes, beating drums and announcing their upcoming performances.
19:26FINN: Interesting. I couldn't imagine that happening now either. But there's also an interesting comparison to make between 18th and 19th century programmes.
19:37MAYA: Wasn't it in the 19th century that theatre programmes started to resemble programmes today? And unlike programmes from the 18th century, they always used colour. And there was a greater variety of designs.
19:52FINN: But personally, I think 18th century programmes were superior because they told the theatre goers so many things including about the actors.
20:02MAYA: And about the writer, the plot, and sometimes the history of the play. That's right. What should we say about theatre programmes in the 20th century?
20:13FINN: I reckon the most important thing is the dramatic change they underwent during World War II, when the government imposed restrictions on the use of paper.
20:23MAYA: Yeah, but that was only in the UK. In the USA, playbills continued to be published in the same format. Well, here in the UK, programs became merely a single sheet of paper folded to create four pages for text. What I don't really get is that after the war, they didn't go back to being more than one sheet, or change in any way for over 25 years. I know there were paper shortages after the war, but only for five or ten years.
20:57FINN: Hmm, strange.
21:02ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 27 to 30.
21:28ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30.
21:35MAYA: I've got some pictures of programs we could include on the slides for our presentation.
21:40FINN: I found a couple too, Maya. Let's go through and see what we think.
21:45MAYA: This is an old one for a play called Ruy Blas. Never heard of that, but the program looks very decorative. Good enough to put in a frame on the wall. The images are just beautiful.
22:00MAYA: Finn, what did you find?
22:02FINN: I've got some pages from a programme for Man of La Mancha. I thought this was a good programme to show... because it contains articles written by members of the theatre company, so we can learn how the production was created and the thoughts and feelings of the cast.
22:21MAYA: Good. I've got a copy of a programme that's now in a museum. It's for The Tragedy of Jane Shore, and it's said to be the earliest surviving document to have been printed on Australia's first printing press.
22:35FINN: Fantastic! Another programme to talk about is for the Sailors Festival. It comes from the British Library's digitised collection of programmes that was started a few years ago. It already comprises over 200,000 programmes. I wish I'd known about it while I was doing my research.
23:01ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 3.
23:03ANNOUNCER: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3.

groups.title: Questions 27–30
groups.instructions:
What comment is made about the programme for each of the following shows?
Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 27–30.

options.text: It is historically significant for a country.
It was effective at attracting audiences.
It is included in a recent project.
It contains insights into the show.

q21.text: Finn was pleased to discover that their topic
options: A. was not familiar to their module leader.
B. had not been chosen by other students.
C. did not prove to be difficult to research.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (had not been chosen by other students)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'No one else on the course is doing the same as us...'

• Phân tích bẫy: Finn thừa nhận việc tìm tài liệu rất khó ('struggled to find many useful websites') nên loại C; chủ đề này chính là lĩnh vực nghiên cứu của giáo viên ('research areas of the module convener') nên loại A.

q22.text: Maya says a mistaken belief about theatre programmes is that
options: A. Theatres pay companies to produce them.
B. Few theatre-goers buy them nowadays.
C. They contain far more adverts than previously.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (Theatres pay companies to produce them)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Contrary to what many people think, theatres don't hire people to do the programmes. In fact, companies buy the rights...'
• Phân tích: Nhiều người lầm tưởng rạp hát trả tiền thuê người làm chương trình ('hire/pay companies'), nhưng thực tế các công ty tự mua quyền in ấn và kiếm tiền từ quảng cáo.

q23.text: Finn was surprised that, in early British theatre, programmes
options: A. were difficult for audiences to obtain.
B. were given out free of charge.
C. were seen as a kind of contract.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (were seen as a kind of contract)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'people accused the theatre of breaking their agreement with the audience. They would demand refunds, and if they didn't get them, there were riots.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'breaking their agreement' = breaching a contract.

q24.text: Maya feels their project should include an explanation of why companies of actors
options: C. had to tour with their plays.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (promoted their own plays)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'lots of ordinary people at that time were illiterate, so theatre programmes were of limited value in advertising plays. When a company of actors arrived in a town, they'd parade around the streets in their costumes, beating drums and announcing their upcoming performances.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'announcing their upcoming performances' = promoted their own plays.

q25.text: Finn and Maya both think that, compared to nineteenth-century programmes, those from the eighteenth century

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (were more informative)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'FINN: 18th century programmes were superior because they told the theatre goers so many things... MAYA: And about the writer, the plot, and sometimes the history of the play. FINN: That's right.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'told so many things... plot, history' = more informative.

q26.text: Maya doesn't fully understand why, in the twentieth century,
options: A. Very few theatre programmes were printed in the USA.
B. British theatre programmes failed to develop for so long.
C. Theatre programmes in Britain copied fashions from the USA

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (British theatre programmes failed to develop for so long)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'What I don't really get is that after the war, they didn't go back to being more than one sheet, or change in any way for over 25 years.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'didn't change in any way for over 25 years' = failed to develop for so long.
• Đáp án đúng: F (It resembles an artwork)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'the program looks very decorative. Good enough to put in a frame on the wall. The images are just beautiful.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'decorative... in a frame on the wall' = resembles an artwork.
• Đáp án đúng: E (It contains insights into the show)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'contains articles written by members of the theatre company, so we can learn how the production was created and the thoughts and feelings of the cast.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'learn how production was created and thoughts/feelings' = insights into the show.
• Đáp án đúng: B (It is historically significant for a country)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'said to be the earliest surviving document to have been printed on Australia's first printing press.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'earliest surviving document on Australia's first printing press' = historically significant for a country.
• Đáp án đúng: D (It is included in a recent project)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'comes from the British Library's digitised collection of programmes that was started a few years ago.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'digitised collection started a few years ago' = recent project.
